held.title: ForType leaks the pairing it built when it then throws ArgumentException.
held.body: `ForType` builds the pairing, with both `FindingDiffAny.Side` objects and the shared interner, before it validates the selection. Two cases then throw `ArgumentException`: selecting a generated row (line 162, which `GeneratedRow_HasNoTypeLevel` exercises) and two selected rows with different identifiers (line 169). In both cases the half-built pairing is dropped without `Release()`. The caller has no reference to it, so it cannot release it either. If `Release` returns pooled or retained backings, as the class's `_released` state suggests, every rejected call leaks them. I could not see what `Release` frees, so I am not sure how much this costs. Fix: wrap the validation after construction in try/catch, and call `pairing.Release()` before rethrowing.
